decisionsTitle: A backoffice table's columns can be resized: the one cost `AdminTable`'s refusal named, paid without the Data Grid
decisionsSection: **The owner, 2026-10-03:** «tabelele ar trebui să folosească MUI Data Grid ca să pot face resize la coloane». What he wants is to resize columns. The data grid was refused when `AdminTable` was built, for four reasons its docstring records and that all still hold: it is a Client Component, so every participant row would cross the server boundary as a prop (`AGENTS.md` §14.5); sorting, filtering and paging would move from the URL into client memory, so a filtered list could no longer be bookmarked or come back after a Server Action redirects; its free tier pages on the client; and the lists would stop working with JavaScript off. That refusal named «no column resizing» as its price. This decision pays that price inside `AdminTable`, with no dependency, and keeps the four reasons. **Decision.** - `AdminTable` takes a `tableId` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; checked, because it becomes a storage key and a CSS selector). Every list names its own: `events`, `pages`, `albums-event`, `albums-free`, `pictures`, `staff`, `registrations`, and one per legal text (`legal-privacy-notice`, …). - The table stays server-rendered. It now emits a `` with one `` per column, the row verbs' last, hidden at the same breakpoints as their cells, so the colgroup and the cells always count the same columns. - Each heading carries one small client island, `ColumnResizeHandle`: the column's right edge, a focusable `role="separator"` (the window-splitter pattern). A pointer drags it; the arrow keys move it 16 px, Shift 64, Home to the column's own floor and End to 960 px; a double click puts that one column back. Its `aria-valuenow` (and `aria-valuetext`, «240 px», from the catalogue: `Admin.columns.widthValue`) is the column's width as laid out now, said again whenever the table is laid out — after a reload with stored widths, a reset, a double click, a breakpoint — not only after a drag; `aria-valuemin` is the column's own floor, also after a reload with stored widths (each fixed layout records the floors it measured, since a resized heading may wrap and can no longer be measured). It receives strings only — the table's id, the column's key, its heading — and lays the table out through the DOM. No row, no render function and no participant data crosses to the client. - No heading word is ever cut. Each column has a floor of its own, measured in the browser while the heading is still one line: the heading's longest word, plus what stays beside the words (the sort arrow, a hint) and the cell's padding — never under 64 px (a 16-px edge to grab, the cell's padding on both sides and a few letters; the per-column floor nearly always dominates). A drag, the arrows and Home stop there, and a stored width under it (the other language's longer word) is raised to it. Once a table is resized its headings wrap between words only. - A resized table switches to `table-layout: fixed` at the sum of its columns: a column nobody dragged keeps the width the automatic layout gives it on today's rows; a long value wraps inside its column and a body cell clips what still does not fit. Wider than the frame, the frame scrolls sideways inside its own border, never the page. - The widths are this browser's own, per table, in `localStorage` under `br.table..widths` (only the columns somebody dragged; an empty entry is removed; a storage that refuses, as in some private windows, reads as nothing stored past the page, while the page itself keeps what it was told, so a second arrow press or drag starts from the first rather than snapping back). A preference about one screen is not something the server, the URL or another organiser needs; a cookie per table read on every request was refused for the same reason. - **Before the first paint.** Right after `` the table carries a few lines of inline script (`ColumnWidthsScript`, the text in `column-widths-script.ts`): it reads `br.table..widths`, measures the columns nobody dragged in the automatic layout, and — when a stored width belongs to a column on screen — appends one `
changelogLine: - **The backoffice tables' columns can be resized** — drag a column's edge in any list (or focus it and use the arrow keys); a column never goes narrower than its heading's longest word, this browser remembers the widths per table and draws them from the first paint, and «Lățimi implicite» puts them back. The tables are still drawn on the server and still work without JavaScript. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a backoffice list at `md` and up with JavaScript on, when a column's edge is dragged or moved with the arrow keys, then that column takes the new width (from its own floor — its heading's longest word with its arrow and padding, never under 64 px — to 960 px, so no heading word is cut), the table switches to a fixed layout whose other columns keep their width, the frame scrolls sideways inside its border rather than the page, and the width is kept for that table in that browser (`br.table.<id>.widths`; for the page alone when storage is refused) until «Lățimi implicite» or a double click on the edge; the edge is a focusable vertical separator named «Lățimea coloanei „…”», one per column but the row verbs', whose `aria-valuenow` is the column's width as laid out now, from the first focus, and whose `aria-valuemin` is that column's floor, after a reload too; with JavaScript off, and on the phone layout, no edge and no reset control is drawn and the table is the automatic one; the edge reaches 44 px under a finger without covering the next heading's sort link; the islands receive the table's id, the column's key and its heading, never a row (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a backoffice table with stored widths, when its page loads, then the stored widths are drawn from the first paint — one inline script right after the table, static but for the table's id, writes one `<style data-column-widths="<id>">` into `<head>` and changes no attribute of the table — and once the page hydrates the islands remove that style and lay the table out themselves, so the table does not jump from the automatic layout to the stored one (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: a backoffice table's columns can be resized
